body.statement:
Yes, with a necessary qualification about what is Gaussian.  Uniformly over triangular arrays in \(\mathcal M_r(\lambda_n)\) satisfying \(\sqrt n\lambda_n\to\infty\), the stacked true-effect cumulant residuals have a first-order influence expansion whose estimated-\(A\) term, with \(C^+=(C^\top C)^{-1}C^\top\), is
\[
 -Q_A\psi^C_{e,n}C^+(m_k-\beta c_k),
\]
and their law is uniformly approximated, in bounded-Lipschitz distance, by a centered Gaussian law on the image of its possibly singular covariance.  The local cumulant-SVD estimator is characterized by the Gaussian-shift argmin relation (14); this is valid under ties, singular covariance, and the boundary \(\beta\in[-B,B]\), whereas an unconditional claim that \(\sqrt n\lambda_n(\widehat\beta-\beta)\) itself is normally distributed is false without an interiority and unique-affine-argmin condition.  A deterministic Anderson--Rubin radius satisfying \(t_{\alpha_0}^2>K_0/\alpha_0\), with \(K_0\) the uniform second-moment constant in (20), makes \(\mathcal C_n\) uniformly asymptotically honest at level \(1-\alpha_0\) without inverting the influence covariance.
body.proof_tex:
The structural target remains \(\beta\), while the observable estimating restrictions are the projected cumulant residuals.  Their relationship is not definitional: the cumulant cancellation identity gives, for every \(k\ge2\),
\[
 m_k-\beta c_k=\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k\in A,
 \qquad
 Q_A(m_k-\beta c_k)=0. \tag{22}
\]
Thus the observable residual vanishes at the causal coefficient because of source independence and the latent-profile-plane restriction.

The uniform generated-projector lemma applies to (22).  It proves equation (10), including the derivative contribution from using the same observations to form \(\widehat C\), \(\widehat Q\), \(\widehat c_k\), and \(\widehat m_k\).  It also proves the uniform Gaussian approximation (13).  Since that argument uses only characteristic functions and positive semidefiniteness, the Gaussian carrier is \(\operatorname{im}(\Sigma_n)\) when \(\Sigma_n\) is singular; no inverse or positive minimum eigenvalue has been introduced.

The local GMM and Anderson--Rubin lemma next substitutes
\[
 b=\beta+\frac{h}{\sqrt n\lambda_n}
\]
into the sample restrictions.  Its equation (18) gives the Gaussian-shift criterion with slopes \(s_{n,k}=Q_Ac_k/\lambda_n\), and the shell condition supplies the indispensable rank statement \(1\le\lVert s_{n,r}\rVert_2\le2\).  This yields tightness of \(\sqrt n\lambda_n(\widehat\beta-\beta)\) and the approximate-argmin equation (14).  That equation retains the interval constraint through \(I_n\), so it remains correct at \(\beta=-B\) or \(\beta=B\), and it does not pretend that a nonsmooth or tied argmin is linear.  When a particular submodel has a unique affine Gaussian argmin, the last implication in the lemma reduces (14) to the usual Gaussian estimator limit; otherwise (14) is the complete computable first-order law.

Finally, (22) makes the Anderson--Rubin statistic at the true causal value exactly the norm-max statistic treated in (20).  Choosing \(t_{\alpha_0}^2>K_0/\alpha_0\) and applying (21) proves uniform asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha_0\).  The calibration is conservative but fully explicit and remains valid when all or part of the Gaussian covariance collapses.  Exact similarity from a single law-independent scalar radius is not asserted: it would require a covariance-dependent quantile and a continuity condition at that quantile.  This proves the stated qualified affirmative answer.
body.justification: This resolves the open proof boundary by giving the same-sample projector correction, a singular Gaussian carrier, the precise Gaussian-driven argmin law, and an explicit uniformly honest Anderson--Rubin calibration.
body.gap: The result proves the generated-projector expansion directly and distinguishes the Gaussian moment process from a generally nonsmooth estimator argmin, avoiding an unsupported universal normality claim.
body.consumer: The expansion and calibration permit singularity-safe uncertainty quantification for weak environmental cumulant flags.
